catalog_quote: Accento. 157. Si arretra di una sillaba in queste voci parossitone: kátara imprecazione κατάρα, ídrota pur del rc. (ὑδρώς -ῶτος), sékli segala n. 139, ćefáloma estremità (κεφαλείωμα) téljoma compimento τελείωμα e múpiamma ammuffimento rc. μουχλίασμα (circa i quali, vedi il n. 159), klóstra filo, legaccio (κλωστήρ -ῆρος), apórga propaggine (ἀπόρρωξ -ῶγος) e kalámippa καλαμίνθη; - e in queste ossitone: khámme χαμαί, dráka (δράξ -κός) less., píra πυρά; oltre che nel tipo di cui sono esempj aréo raro ἀραιός, oddío ἐλειός, anizzío ἀνεψιός (cfr. il dialetto di Patmos e l'antico eolico, Mull. 93), laddove nel comune romaico è all'incontro norma costante che -io[s] -ia passino in -ió[s] -iá. ... 158. Si arretra poi l'accento di due sillabe, in damásino prugna rc. δαμασκηνόν, prástiko πρακτικός. — 159. Progredisce l'acc. di una sill., dalla terzultima alla penult., in: akrivía scarsità, scrupolosità ἀκρίβεια, afudía βοήθεια, apovráma (ἀπόβρεγμα), konída lendine κόνιδα, asteríga rc. πτεροῦγα (πτέρυξ), vrísma ὕβρισμα, guámma cacciata rc. ἔβγαλμα e guémma uscita *ἔκβημα, nóma ὄνομα ...; - dalla penultima all'ultima, in akomí ancora rc. ἀκόμι, prosté 'avantjeri' pur. rc. προχθές (πρόχθες); - dalla terzult. all'ultima: traganó 'duro, forte', rc. τράγανος, zarfó ἐξάδελφος, rukanikó rc. ῥουκάνικον (lat. lucanica salsiccia), sekamenó συκάμινος, to imisí la metà ἥμισυς, ecc. ... Le alterazioni dell'acc. nella flessione, concordano colle comuni romaiche.

(ὑδρώς -ῶτος), sékli segala [...] e in queste ossitone: khámme χαμαί, dráka (δράξ -κός) less., píra πυρά [...]. 158. Si arretra poi l'accento di due sillabe, in damásino prugna rc. δαμασκηνόν, prástiko πρακτικός. — 159. Progredisce l'acc. di una sill., dalla terzultima alla penult., in: akrivía scarsità, scrupolosità ἀκρίβεια [...]; dalla penultima all'ultima, in akomí ancora rc. ἀκόμι [...]; dalla terzult. all'ultima: traganó 'duro, forte' [...]. new_statements.translation: Accent. 157. It retracts by one syllable in these paroxytone words: kátara 'curse' κατάρα, ídrota (also in Modern Greek, ὑδρώς), sékli 'rye' [...] and in these oxytones: khámme χαμαί, dráka, píra πυρά [...]. 158. The accent retracts by two syllables in damásino 'plum' (MG δαμασκηνόν), prástiko (πρακτικός). — 159. The accent advances by one syllable, from the antepenult to the penult, in akrivía 'scarcity, scrupulousness' (ἀκρίβεια) [...]; from the penult to the final syllable in akomí 'still' (MG ἀκόμι) [...]; from the antepenult to the final: traganó 'hard, strong' [...]. The alterations of the accent in inflection agree with those of common Modern Greek.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent in Bova (Calabrian) Greek is the inherited Greek lexical accent: Morosi gives no positional rule, only a list of individual words whose accent has retracted or advanced relative to common Modern Greek, and states that accent alternations within inflection follow Modern Greek (i.e. the Greek pattern of mobile stress within the final three syllables, e.g. antepenultimate stress in past-tense forms, penult shift in proparoxytone plurals). Supporting first-hand statements from saved files: Morosi 1870: VII (Salento) marks accent on all words of more than two syllables and on oxytone disyllables, leaving paroxytone disyllables unmarked, i.e. treats stress as lexically distinctive with penult as the unmarked disyllabic pattern; Koutsoukos 2013: 127 'Past tense verbal forms in SMG and Modern Greek dialects are characterized by having antepenultimate stress.. The data from Griko shows exactly the same phonological rule (Morosi, 1870): pesíniska'; Stamuli 2008: 150 fn. 107 refers to 'la fonematicità della posizione dell'accento'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: Morosi 1878 §§157-159 list ~30 lexical items whose accent position differs from Modern Greek (retraction by one or two syllables, advancement to penult or final); §187 (p. ~40): in masculine proparoxytones the Modern Greek plural accent shift is 'non costante' (átropo pl. atrópi, but ánghelo pl. ángheli, mástora pl. mástori). Morosi 1870 (Salento): plural of proparoxytones shifts accent to the penult 'alla dorica' (antrópi < ántropo); enclitic object pronouns move the accent (guàlo+me > gualóme); footnote 137 in Koutsoukos: mediopassive imperfect has penultimate stress (koimómoun). Turturro 2020: 44 notes frequent accent shifts vs. Greek etyma in written Griko (kardìa, travudì, òria, pedìa).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (citation forms and inflected forms in the grammar sketch); Morosi 1878 describes the Bova dialect of Calabria; Morosi 1870 and Koutsoukos 2013 describe Salentine Griko. No modern phonological description with an explicit synchronic rule (trisyllabic window etc.) was opened; the reading 'lexical' is inferred from these sources' treatment of accent as an etymological, distinctive, morphologically mobile property.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog apul1236 'Apulia-Calabrian Greek' lumps two Italiot Greek varieties: Salentine Griko (Grecìa Salentina, Lecce) and Calabrian Greko/Grecanico (Bovesìa, Aspromonte). The quoted statement (Morosi 1878) describes the Bova dialect of Calabria; the supporting statements (Morosi 1870, Koutsoukos 2013, Turturro 2020) describe Salentine Griko; Stamuli 2008 describes Bovesìa. Both varieties show the same Greek-type lexical accent. No separate Glottolog codes exist for the two varieties (hh.bib uses NOCODE_Calabrian-Greek for both).

sources.note: 'Accidenti generali: Accento' §§157-159 (pp. 29-30): accent is the inherited Greek lexical accent; lists words where it retracts one or two syllables or advances (antepenult>penult, penult>final, antepenult>final) relative to common Modern Greek; 'Le alterazioni dell'acc. nella flessione, concordano colle comuni romaiche' (p. 30); §187 (p. ~40): in masc. proparoxytones the plural accent retraction of Modern Greek is not constant (átropo, pl. atrópi but ánghelo pl. ángheli).

sources.citation: Koutsoukos, Nikolaos. 2013. A constructionist view of complex interactions between inflection and derivation: the case of SMG and Griko. PhD thesis, University of Patras.
sources.note: p. 127: 'Past tense verbal forms in Standard Modern Greek (henceforth SMG) and Modern Greek dialects are characterized by having antepenultimate stress.. The data from Griko shows exactly the same phonological rule (Morosi, 1870): pesíniska 1SG IMP < pesinísko die'; p. 93: Karanastasis (1997: 83ff.) divides Griko verbs into two conjugations by non-final vs final stress of the citation form (alatídzo vs omiló, agapó); stress is treated as lexically/morphologically determined, not positional.

sources.citation: Stamuli, Maria Francesca. 2008. Morte di lingua e variazione lessicale nel greco di Calabria. Tre profili dalla Bovesìa. PhD thesis, Università di Napoli Federico II.
